criteria: results/selection_criteria.md (committed 50da184 before step-6 runs): 1 Context Evidence Rate, 2 grounded mean, 3 abstention then false abstention, 4 cost then latency; a gap of <=1 question to the best is a tie.
application: Step 1 CER: best 21/21; keep >=20: dense-B-k3, hybrid-B-k3, hybrid-B-k5, hybrid-B-k3-think, hybrid-B-k5-think. Drop bm25-B-k3 (19/21).
Step 2 grounded: best 20 questions graded 2; dense-B-k3 and hybrid-B-k5-think have 19 (1 question) -> tie, all kept.
Step 3 abstention: best 3/3 (hybrid-B-k5-think); keep >=2/3: dense-B-k3, hybrid-B-k5, hybrid-B-k3-think, hybrid-B-k5-think. Drop hybrid-B-k3 (1/3). False abstention 0/21 for all.
Step 4 cost: dense-B-k3 $0.0231 < hybrid-B-k5 $0.0352 < hybrid-B-k3-think $0.0394 < hybrid-B-k5-think $0.0456.
conclusion: On 21+3 dev questions no improvement beats the baseline by more than 1 question on any quality criterion, and the baseline is the cheapest of the remaining candidates, so the pre-declared rule selects the baseline.

comparison_arm.why: Winner of the same rule when the baseline is excluded (steps 1-3 tie, cheapest of hybrid-B-k5 / k3-think / k5-think). Declared before any test run so test can compare baseline vs an improvement; its test result does NOT change the selection.

test_protocol: Run src.run_agent once on split test for configs/dense-B-k3.json and configs/hybrid-B-k5.json, plus src.eval_retrieval --split test for the same methods. No config, prompt, code or label-rule change after viewing test. Manually label every test question (9 answerable + 3 abstain) for both arms, including context grade 0/1/2.
